# ISSUE-402 implementation plan

Register coordinator-owned durable use before touching managed storage, and retain it through the last consumer. This is the producer-coverage prerequisite for reclamation, not a new cache deletion command. Preserve the existing `swarm issue cleanup --all-merged` authorization and merge-evidence path.

## Recorded maintainer decision

The CHANGES_REQUESTED decision replaces the previous descendant-proof requirement and process-containment reopen condition. Use existing stronger completion proof where available, including the Bubblewrap executor PID namespace. For native Codex, host validation and host prefetch, command exit plus successful `process.StopVerified` counts as finished. This applies to verified cleanup after nonzero exit or cancellation as well; cancellation without a verified stop, failed or uncertain stops, and coordinator crashes retain pending evidence. Complete coordinator observation, import and other resource consumers before finishing the scope. Ordinary completed runs must leave no pending records. No containment work is planned.

Update the `Use.Finish` doc comment and `SECURITY.md` to state plainly: a process that deliberately detaches into its own session is not tracked and cleanup may remove a cache under it; it keeps only its existing sandbox access. Keep `TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer` as documentation of this accepted limit, not an implementation blocker. All other design and acceptance coverage below stands.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; execution profile: sensitive; plan gate: human. Estimated cycle: 10–14 hours within the 16-hour total claim budget, including independent review and focused race checks. No protected harness changes. Linux and macOS host storage for native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap are covered; OCI garbage collection and remote archival remain out of scope.

## What we know

- `internal/storageuse/storage.go:225` persists a pending token before resource creation. Existing storage starts with incomplete legacy coverage; `Finish` at line 267 currently requires proof all consumers exited; its doc comment must change to the recorded completion contract. `AcquireMaintenance` at line 307 rejects incomplete coverage and pending tokens while holding admission locked. Existing crash and surviving-child tests are in `internal/storageuse/crash_unix_test.go:21` and `:84`.
- Repository build keys hash the canonical Git common directory (`internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:111`); preparation and legacy Go migration currently create/move storage without durable use (`:155`, `:224`). Production search found no `AcquireUse` calls outside storageuse; inventory only observes registrations (`internal/storage/inventory.go:264`).
- Dependency preparation creates ecosystem directories before prefetch, including the marker-hit read path (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:254`). Go/Rust, Python and Node prefetch scratch lives in `dependency_cache.go:587`, `:1031`, `dependency_cache_python.go:59`, and `node_prefetch.go:86`.
- Native/delegated runs share `withNativeWorkspaceClock` (`internal/sandbox/native.go:639`); cache creation occurs inside run callbacks (`native.go:537`, `delegated.go:170`). Its scratch survives through observation, timeout recovery and import. Reviewer snapshots add an outer lifetime (`internal/agent/review.go:32`).
- Validation prepares caches once and shares them across warm-up and checks (`internal/validation/validator.go:324`); trusted-base warm-up and marker writes are in `internal/validation/build_cache.go:48`. Repair creates another temporary checkout (`internal/validation/repair.go:493`).
- `process.StopVerified` checks process-group kill only (`internal/process/tree_unix.go:18`). It does not track deliberately detached sessions. The maintainer accepts command exit plus successful StopVerified for host completion; update the conflicting Finish comment. `internal/sandbox/native_completion_unix_test.go:24` documents the detached-child limit; preserve its assertions. Host prefetch (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:555`) and host validation (`internal/validation/validator.go:647`) currently call unchecked Stop and need verified-stop result plumbing. Bubblewrap uses `--unshare-all` and `--die-with-parent` (`internal/sandbox/executor.go:61`); preserve its stronger boundary.
- Inventory identities are `cache:<absolute path>` or `scratch:<absolute path>`; cache classes distinguish agent/validator build/dependency ownership (`internal/storage/discovery.go:197`). Indexed inventory currently rejects scratch classes (`internal/storage/indexed.go:13`). CLI reporting does not yet supply UseRoot (`internal/cli/storage.go:31`).
- Bulk cleanup already delegates to the single-issue apply path (`internal/cli/cleanup_bulk.go:59`, `internal/cli/cleanup.go:105`); preserve it. Its tests cover fresh apply evidence and mixed eligibility.
- The slash command requires these two artifacts only (`.claude/commands/swarm-plan.md`). No implementation, staging, approval or publication is part of this planner run.

## What we're assuming

- Trusted host user-cache control storage can be shared by all coordinator entry points without granting it to workers. Check with path-overlap fixtures and mount/argv/environment assertions before wiring consumers.
- Canonical repository ownership can be resolved from trusted coordinator inputs for GitHub and local backends, including linked worktrees and detached review/warm-up copies. Resolve from the original repository before creating snapshots; never hash a temporary snapshot as the repository identity.
- Completion status can be carried in coordinator-only memory separately from the command error. Check every runner return path: a nonzero command result or cancellation must not hide a successful verified stop, and a nil result must never hide a failed stop. Ordinary completed runs must finish durable uses; unresolved stops retain them.

## Open questions

- Parent #378 sections A–D are not present in this sandbox; no connected issue tool was available. The WorkUnit remains authoritative. The reviewer should compare the coverage table below against that parent context; implementation can verify the enumerated local producers without waiting for remote access.
- This exported snapshot has no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). Approved-base absence of the intended issue fragment cannot be established here. Step 1 must check the approved base before describing any production file as new. All listed Go/docs/test files already exist and are modified, not new.
- Which call sites currently discard stop errors or conflate command failure with stop failure? Steps 2–5 audit and carry completion status under the recorded decision. This is lifecycle plumbing, not a requirement to prove detached descendants ended or to add containment.
- Inspection/canary runs can precede repository selection. Step 1 assigns a trusted host-scope identity for those runs, with unknown repository eligibility; lack of a repository must never authorize deletion.

## Architectural design and exact touchpoints

Use `internal/storageuse/storage.go` for a coordinator-only scope that owns the Manager and a set of durable Use handles. Add resource construction and managed temporary allocation helpers in that existing file. Resolve a single private host control root using trusted coordinator configuration of the user cache, separate from resource roots and all sandbox grants. Do not introduce a config key, environment override, worker protocol field, or CLI option for this root. Share its resolution with report wiring; an absent root remains a read-only unknown observation.

Use canonical trusted repository ownership, exact class, exact clean absolute location and the existing inventory identity format as the resource key. Centralize construction so admission and observation cannot diverge. Preserve agent-build / validate-build / agent-deps / validate-deps / legacy-go-build and scratch ownership distinctions. Never allow candidate manifests, custom cache env values or contents to choose a control root or authorize maintenance. Shared user-owned host caches and credentials remain outside reclamation scope.

Pass coordinator scopes in process memory through existing context plumbing, never through serialized WorkerOptions, Dependencies, sandbox arguments, environment, MCP tools or artifacts. A scope used by workflow prefetch must live across all later role consumers, not end when preparation returns. Separate invocations reacquire read use before accessing already prepared resources. Do not store completion authority in a worker-visible Dependencies value.

| Resource / operation | Admission boundary | Scope ends only after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agent/validator ecosystem build cache | before directory creation, migration, reads or writes | last run/check and coordinator inspection complete, under the recorded completion contract |
| legacy Go source and destination | both admitted in deterministic identity order before rename | migration operations finish; source stays legacy-unknown and destination inherits unknown provenance |
| agent/validator dependency cache | before mkdir, preflight cache reads, marker reads, prefetch or marker writes | prefetch and every sandbox reader of the returned cache complete |
| per-run build fallback/overlay | outer scratch admitted before creation; nested cache lifetime covered by that root | all overlay users, observers, recovery and import finish |
| prefetch scratch, including sibling Rust scratch | allocate random name, persist use, then exclusively create with safefs | fetch processes and coordinator copies finish; uncertain termination leaves unresolved |
| native workspace/control/scratch | before allocation and archive work | process completion, session observation, output import and timeout recovery finish |
| reviewer snapshot | before snapshot creation | nested run plus artifact collection complete |
| validation home, warm-up and repair checkout | before allocation or worktree creation | warm-up, all checks, fast/full passes, base reruns and teardown complete |
| native/delegated inspection and executor/overlay canary scratch | before allocation | all probe processes and inspection reads complete; repository-less evidence remains conservative |

For temporary allocation, avoid `MkdirTemp` followed by admission (too late for complete coverage): choose a cryptographically random basename, admit the exact absent root, then create exclusively through a root-bound helper. If a collision occurs, retain conservative evidence and retry a different identity; never mark someone else's existing directory covered. All normal teardown must be root-bound and leave recovery output needed by unfinished work intact. Pending evidence survives coordinator crash, failed completion writes and failed or unverified stops under the recorded contract. Completion uses a bounded independent context after the recorded completion contract and remaining coordinator consumers are satisfied so cancellation cannot silently erase the obligation; failures propagate or are reported with the primary failure preserved.

## Implementation sequence

1. Audit the table against all production `MkdirTemp`, cache preparation, marker and consumer call sites. Confirm approved-base status of `changes/unreleased/402.md`; modify it if present, otherwise create the child fragment. Establish resource identity/control-root helpers and coordinator scope semantics in `internal/storageuse/storage.go` and extend `storage_test.go` and `crash_unix_test.go`. Update the `Use.Finish` doc comment at `internal/storageuse/storage.go:265` to the recorded contract and detached-session limit; keep locking, record format and durable admission semantics unchanged.
2. Modify `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go`, `dependency_cache.go`, `dependency_cache_python.go`, and `node_prefetch.go`: acquire before any resource touch, protect migration source and destination, retain unknown provenance across migration, register prefetch scratch, and carry dependency uses beyond return. Durable-admission failures stop access; they must not be swallowed by existing best-effort persistent-cache fallback. A scratch fallback is allowed only when separately admitted safely. Marker hits also acquire use. Replace unchecked host prefetch Stop with StopVerified and preserve completion status independently of fetch errors. Extend the corresponding existing tests, including successful prefetch and marker-hit runs with zero pending records.
3. Modify `internal/sandbox/native.go`, `delegated.go`, `executor.go`, and `validation.go`, plus `internal/agent/review.go` and `isolated.go`: cover managed workspace/probe/snapshot scratch and all cache readers, callbacks, MCP execution and overlay consumers. Observe and import before finishing. Accept command exit plus successful StopVerified for host runs, retaining existing stronger Bubblewrap PID-namespace completion. Preserve sandbox policy and process-group strategy; no containment changes. Carry stop verification separately from command success/cancellation so failed or uncertain stops retain pending evidence. Extend native/executor/review tests with held-reader barriers and ordinary-completion zero-pending assertions; preserve `internal/sandbox/native_completion_unix_test.go` and `TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer` unchanged as the detached-session limitation fixture.
4. Modify `internal/workflow/dependencies.go`, `engine.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_implementation.go`, and `execute_validation.go` only at scope ownership/call sites: keep preflight/role/reviewer dependency use live across engine returns and cancellation paths; independently invoked roles reacquire before reads. Scope ownership must handle pre-claim preflight errors without creating claim authority. Extend `dependencies_test.go` and existing workflow lifecycle fixtures.
5. Modify `internal/validation/build_cache.go`, `validator.go`, and `repair.go`: carry validator scopes across preparation, warm-up marker hits/writes, all candidate checks, retries, diagnostic base reruns, and checkout teardown. Keep trusted-base policy loading and cache mount selection unchanged. Replace unchecked host check Stop with StopVerified and propagate its verified completion status separately from check outcome. Extend existing build-cache, dependency-cache and repair tests, including zero pending records after ordinary warm-up, checks and diagnostic reruns.
6. Modify `internal/storage/discovery.go`, `indexed.go`, `inventory.go` and `internal/cli/storage.go` only to reconcile shared identities and observe the trusted use root, including indexed managed scratch with layout validation. Never recurse into arbitrary registered paths. Unknown/orphan/legacy data stays unknown. Preserve report's bounded read-only behavior. No reclaim flag or second eligibility path; existing cleanup command/help remain unchanged. Extend `internal/storage/discovery_test.go`, `inventory_test.go`, `internal/cli/storage_test.go`, and retain cleanup regression coverage.
7. Modify `SECURITY.md:86` (build/dependency storage discussion) to explain the recorded completion rule, stronger Bubblewrap namespace proof, interrupted-use retention and the exact detached-session limit above. Keep prose practical and preserve existing access boundaries. Update existing `docs/project.md` managed-storage paragraphs to explain coordinator registration and conservative interrupted/legacy retention, without promising new deletion behavior. Add/update `changes/unreleased/402.md` following the base check. Run the focused verification in TEST_PLAN.md and obtain independent sensitive-boundary review.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved contracts, policy, gates or validation.

- Entry points: `storageuse.AcquireUse` / `Use.Finish` / `AcquireMaintenance` (`internal/storageuse/storage.go:225`, `:267`, `:307`); `PrepareBuildCaches` and `migrateLegacyGoCache` (`internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:155`, `:224`); `PrepareDependencyCaches` (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:254`); `withNativeWorkspaceClock` (`internal/sandbox/native.go:639`); `RunDelegatedHarness` (`internal/sandbox/delegated.go:125`); `RunReview` (`internal/agent/review.go:32`); `Engine.AgentDependencies` (`internal/workflow/dependencies.go:33`); `Validate` and `runCheck` (`internal/validation/validator.go:210`, `:598`); `warmBuildCaches` (`internal/validation/build_cache.go:48`); `baseRerun.prepare` (`internal/validation/repair.go:493`); `scanner.indexed` (`internal/storage/indexed.go:13`).
- Fixtures to extend: existing storageuse crash/surviving-child and admission barriers; sandbox fake prefetch and owner-path fixtures; native/executor cache-reuse and boundary fixtures; reviewer hostile-output fixtures; workflow dependency preflight fixtures; validation cache/repair fixtures; storage read-only and bounded inventory fixtures. Preserve all existing adversarial assertions.
- Exact focused commands are the developer command block in TEST_PLAN.md. Tester independently verifies source/lifetimes and reuses applicable passing results. Do not edit `internal/cli` test `TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery`: operator reports a known main failure unrelated to this task.
- Checked assumptions: cache identity is based on the Git common directory, confirmed by source; dependency scope must outlive preparation, confirmed by workflow RunRequest call sites; process-group cleanup misses deliberately detached sessions, confirmed by `tree_unix.go` and the existing native completion fixture; the recorded maintainer decision accepts this limit and supersedes the old Finish comment. Approved-base fragment absence and parent context remain unverified as stated above.
- Reopen the plan if complete coverage requires new sandbox permissions, credential forwarding, protected policy edits, a new cleanup eligibility path, deletion/recovery of unresolved records, or a storageuse record-format migration. The detached-session limit and lack of containment are settled by the maintainer decision and do not reopen this plan. Do not add containment work. Recommend a separate WorkUnit rather than expanding other areas. Reassess budget if the producer audit uncovers another independent storage subsystem.
- **What this change breaks:** searches found PrepareBuildCaches callers/tests in sandbox native/executor and validation; preserve signatures where possible and update tests for required coordinator scope. PrepareDependencyCaches callers in workflow/dependencies.go and validation/build_cache.go must share lifetime ownership; update both and their stubs. `Dependencies` is passed to workflow role requests: preserve its worker-visible data-only contract. Tests `TestNativeCodexAgentBuildCacheReuse`, `TestBubblewrapAgentBuildCacheReuse`, `TestBubblewrapValidationBuildCacheIsolation`, `TestBubblewrapCandidateWritesDiscarded`, `TestDependencyCachePathAndOwners`, `TestDependencyCacheNoFallback`, and `TestGoPrefetchMarkerSkipsRepeat` must retain their original security/cache expectations while adding admission evidence. `internal/storage/indexed.go` currently rejects scratch: update only the trusted managed-layout cases and preserve arbitrary-class/path rejection. `docs/project.md` manually advises stopping consumers before cache removal: preserve safe manual advice and clarify automatic evidence retention. `docs/developer.md:88`, `internal/cli/cleanup.go:105`, `cleanup_bulk.go:59`, and all cleanup authorization/head-fencing tests preserve unchanged. `Use.Finish` callers must use the revised completion contract; modify its conflicting comment without changing record semantics. `SECURITY.md:86` gains the explicit completion and detached-session limit; preserve all other security boundaries. Preserve `TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer` unchanged. Protected files, existing changelog fragments and the known failing CLI test preserve unchanged.

## Operator guidance

> Apply the maintainer's recorded decision on use completion; it replaces the plan's statements that StopVerified is insufficient and its process-containment reopen condition. Add SECURITY.md and the Use.Finish comment to the touchpoints.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

# ISSUE-402 focused test plan

## Completion contract for all cases

Apply the recorded maintainer decision: use Bubblewrap PID-namespace completion where available; native Codex, host validation and host prefetch finish after command exit plus successful `process.StopVerified`, followed by remaining coordinator consumers. Command failure is distinct from stop failure. Failed or uncertain stops, crashes and cancellation without verified stop retain pending evidence. No containment work or detached-session proof is required.

For each native, delegated/Bubblewrap, reviewer, host prefetch (each ecosystem and marker-hit path), validation warm-up/check/repair and workflow-owned dependency path, add an ordinary-completion case asserting **zero pending use records** after the full scope ends. Check the durable records themselves, not just maintenance denial (legacy coverage can independently deny maintenance). Include nonzero command exit with verified stop, cancellation with verified stop, cancellation without verified stop, and injected stop/Finish-write failures. Maintenance must remain blocked while any tracked consumer or coordinator observer/import is held. Fresh, fully covered resources become eligible after completion; legacy resources remain unknown even with no pending tokens.

Preserve `TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer` and its detached-write assertions as documentation of the accepted limit. It must pass without requiring the detached child to end before native command return. Existing crash/surviving-child tests continue to prove that unresolved uses are not cleared after restart.

## Acceptance mapping

| WorkUnit acceptance criterion | Cases and evidence | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Cover creation, migration, reads, writes, prefetch and validation with matching resource identities and complete consumer lifetimes. | Table-driven producer audit covers agent/validator build and dependency ecosystems; legacy migration source+destination; prefetch miss/hit; native and delegated readers; scratch fallback and overlay; reviewer snapshot; warm-up, marker hit, candidate checks, fast/full checks and diagnostic reruns. Capture the exact Resource at the producer barrier and compare to inventory observation, including linked issue/PR worktrees and snapshots. Verify registration precedes first mkdir/read/write/rename and lasts beyond preparation return until the last consumer/observer/import ends. Exercise local and GitHub coordinator fixtures. Repository-less probes remain conservatively owned. | Commands A, B, C below; source coverage table reviewed by tester. |
| 2. Prove maintenance exclusion with barriers and preserve unresolved crash and legacy evidence. | Hold barriers at pre-create, migration rename, prefetch write, cached read, validation warm-up/read, process exit, observer/import and final completion. Concurrent AcquireMaintenance must fail while use is pending; with maintenance held, canceled admission cannot touch storage. Multiple coordinators retain every token; after completion under the recorded contract maintenance succeeds only for fresh complete resources. Kill coordinator with a surviving child and an unfinished use; after restart no timeout/PID/lease/closed-issue inference completes use. Preexisting, missing/corrupt record, migration, collision, failed admission/Finish and canceled cleanup remain unknown/pending. Retain existing crash tests. | A, B, C; existing subprocess fixtures on Unix; unsupported runtime cases enter PR checklist. |
| 3. Preserve sandbox grants, credentials and agent-validator ownership separation. | Assert control roots/tokens never occur in worker mounts, argv, env, archives, MCP inputs or cache contents. Reject symlinked control root/parents, root overlap, alias/traversal/special files and path replacement. Malicious manifests/cache markers cannot authorize maintenance. Cache ecosystem/path identity cannot merge repositories or owners. Candidates still cannot write validator persistent caches; dependencies remain read-only; warm-up reads approved base. Existing no-fallback, credential-filter, native/executor boundary and cleanup authorization/fence tests remain intact. Report does not create control storage or mutate evidence and remains bounded. | A, B, C, D; independent source review of data flow and grants. |
| 4. Pass focused race tests, preserve existing adversarial tests and add a child changelog fragment. | Passing race results for changed production packages and cross-package coverage above; no deleted/weakened adversarial tests. Child fragment `changes/unreleased/402.md` passes existing checker. Verify base existence before classifying fragment new/modified. Review the revised Use.Finish comment and SECURITY.md for the accepted completion rule and explicit detached-session/cache-removal limit; docs/examples/help still match existing CLI. | A–E; tester reviews diff and results. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Use scratch-backed Go build/temp caches permitted by the environment. These commands are intended for the implementation checkout with Git metadata. Run each applicable command once after relevant edits; repeat only for relevant source changes, observed failures or an unresolved coverage concern. Record command, revision/source state, result, duration and environmental skips.

```bash
# A: durable evidence and read-only identity integration
 go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage -count=1
# Explicit accepted-limit regression (also included in B)
 go test -race -timeout=1m ./internal/sandbox -run '^TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer$' -count=1
# B: changed sandbox, agent, workflow and validation lifetimes and existing adversarial cases
 go test -race -timeout=10m ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation -count=1
# C: CLI report and existing cleanup eligibility/authorization regression fixtures
 go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/cli -run '^Test.*(Storage|Cleanup).*$' -count=1
# D: changed-package static diagnostics and formatting (read-only)
 go vet ./internal/storageuse ./internal/storage ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/validation ./internal/cli
 gofmt -l internal/storageuse internal/storage internal/sandbox internal/agent internal/workflow internal/validation internal/cli
# E: child fragment, help and documentation contract
 go run ./cmd/changelog --check
 go run ./cmd/swarm issue cleanup --help
 go run ./cmd/swarm storage report --help
```

Formatting output must be empty for changed files; fix only task-owned changes. If B exceeds its timeout, use test-name groups within those packages rather than deleting cases; document the grouping. Existing environment-dependent sandbox tests may skip unavailable boundaries; list the skips explicitly for maintainer verification. Add deterministic channel/pipe barriers and subprocess handshakes instead of sleeps. Each security regression must fail against the prior behavior; where feasible demonstrate this by running the new fixture against an isolated base checkout without modifying protected files.

The operator reports `internal/cli TestIssuePlanReplanCapAndRecovery` already failing on main. Do not edit it, weaken it, or use it to justify unrelated fixes. C deliberately selects storage/cleanup tests. If coordinator verification encounters the known failure, record it separately with the operator attribution and any available base evidence; do not claim the full suite passed.

## Tester-owned independent review and result reuse

Independently trace the source against every row of the plan's producer coverage table. Audit all production temp allocation, cache mkdir/read/write, migration, marker-hit and Dependencies consumer call sites, including workflow preflight outside claims and independent reviewer runs. Confirm original repository identity survives snapshots and that every early return and cancellation distinguishes verified completion from an unresolved stop; panic/crash and unverified-stop paths retain evidence. Review completion status against the recorded contract: command exit plus successful StopVerified is sufficient on host paths; retain stronger Bubblewrap namespace proof. A deferred Finish alone is insufficient. Independently confirm zero pending records for every ordinary-completion path and retention for unverified stops/crashes. Confirm host prefetch and validation no longer discard stop verification failures. Review Use.Finish and SECURITY.md together for the deliberate-detach limit: cleanup may remove a cache beneath that process, which keeps only its existing sandbox access.

Inspect the complete diff for unchanged mount policy, credential filters, approved-base loading, cache ownership, safefs root binding, recovery preservation, cleanup authorization/reservation/claim/expected-head behavior and adversarial test assertions. Ensure no new deletion operation or bypass was introduced. Compare the coverage audit with parent #378 sections A–D when available; flag contract-relevant omissions.

Reuse applicable passing developer results tied to the final source. Run only missing tests or tests invalidated by relevant edits, observed failure or a specific unresolved coverage concern. Independently inspect barrier assertions and escaped-child fixtures even when reusing their passing runs. Report each criterion as met, failed or environment-limited with concrete evidence.

## Coordinator-owned policy reference

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once after roles finish. The compiled policy in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md is the reference; it is not a developer/tester execution checklist. Agent results are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. Preserve the human plan gate and do not request coordinator credentials, approve the plan, stage, renew or publish from these checks.

## PR review checklist for unavailable environments

- Verify Linux native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap real-process/cache-grant cases skipped by sandbox restrictions; include surviving descendants and cancellation while tools are active.
- Verify macOS native Codex and platform-dependent private-root/temporary-path behavior, including temporary-directory aliases. Bubblewrap coverage is Linux; do not claim it runs on macOS.
- Run local and GitHub backend fixture coverage in the implementation checkout; only a missing live-service check belongs to maintainer follow-through, never a prerequisite for implementing fixture coverage.
- Confirm intended fragment path against the approved base (Git metadata is absent in the planner snapshot), links/anchors for changed docs, Bash snippet syntax if edited, and existing help names/options. No new command or flag is planned.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> Apply the maintainer's recorded decision on use completion; it replaces the plan's statements that StopVerified is insufficient and its process-containment reopen condition. Add SECURITY.md and the Use.Finish comment to the touchpoints.

<!-- swarm:guidance:end -->

Failed or uncertain stops, crashes and cancellation without a verified stop retain pending evidence. Keep TestNativeCommandSuccessCanLeaveStorageConsumer as documentation of that limit. Ordinary completed runs must leave no pending records, with tests per path. No containment work. Rest of the design stands.

# PR #405 regression revision plan

Plan only the two operator-reported regressions. ORIGINAL_PLAN.md and ORIGINAL_TEST_PLAN.md remain the approved design and unchanged coverage; ACCEPTED_REVISIONS.md contains no additional deltas. Approved dimensions remain multi_area / known / sensitive, with a human gate. Estimated revision cycle: 3–6 hours within the 16-hour budget. No production changes or tests are executed during this planning phase.

## What we know

- `internal/sandbox/build_cache_test.go:455` (`buildCacheRoles`) passes nonexistent role children of scratch to `agentBuildCaches`. `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:174` (`scratchBuildCache`) opens the scratch root with `Sub(..., false, ...)`, intentionally requiring it to exist. The two reported isolation tests call this shared fixture at lines 532 and 561. Preserve that production precondition and all policy assertions.
- `internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:610` allocates prefetch scratch and defers `Scope.CleanupTemp` into its named result. `internal/storageuse/storage.go:696` marks the scope retained but also joins every removal failure into the operation error. `internal/safefs/root.go:353` (`RemoveAllChecked`) checks the direct child's identity and calls root-bound removal without read-only-directory handling.
- CI.md quotes check 124559364028, published head ef6f73cfaf59c1bdd7dd5d39aad209cf22fce438: core-regressions failed at `TestRepairClassifiesRegression`, repair_test.go:53, because prefetch scratch removal returned directory-not-empty. This is diagnostic evidence; the operator identifies read-only module directories as the cause. PR_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md contains no review evidence.
- `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go:481` tests replacement, symlink, uncertain-stop and panic retention, including errors for identity substitution. Preserve those assertions. The checkout has no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails); every proposed production/test touchpoint below already exists, and no new file is planned.

## What we're assuming

Read-only nested module directories explain the CI removal error. Confirm cheaply with a deterministic nested 0555-directory/0444-file module fixture before fixing cleanup; run as an ordinary user so privilege cannot hide the failure. No Go invocation or network is needed for that fixture.

## Open questions

The exact safe permission primitive depends on the pinned-directory APIs available in this Go version. During step 2 confirm permissions can be changed on an opened, identity-checked real directory without following links or substituted parents. If existing primitives cannot guarantee this, add the smallest descriptor-based safefs implementation in its existing platform files; do not weaken confinement. Platform cases unavailable here receive fixture coverage and a maintainer review note, not an implementation blocker.

## Revision changes
